facts.raw_span: A 29-year-old man was referred for left ptosis and diplopia
Six months earlier, his car had crashed into a roadside tree
he developed orthostatic headaches and malaise
an increasing difficulty opening his eyes
an out-of-focus feeling that worsened after waking and improved after lying down
best-corrected visual acuity was 1.5 in both eyes
the pupillary light reflexes were normal
There was no limitation of extraocular movements
alternate prism cover testing revealed 8 prism diopters of left exotropia and 4 prism diopters of right exotropia at distance
Slit-lamp and fundus examinations were unremarkable
Routine blood tests were normal
both the anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody and the edrophonium tests were negative
